bull_bear.body:
- Contracted software development revenue is recognised at prices determined per client contract, indicating a contract-based rather than spot revenue base (auditors' key audit matter on revenue recognition)
- Loyalty programme relationships with banks and financial institutions, a client set with high switching costs once a rewards platform is embedded (auditors' key audit matter)

- Recently completed IPO and BSE listing (25.03.2026) provides listed-company access to capital
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Revenue recognition on contract software development is a key audit matter — The auditors flagged the amount of revenue recognition as a key audit matter under SA 701, since software applications are developed for various clients at prices determined per contract. The auditors had to involve IT specialists to test the design and operating effectiveness of key IT controls over revenue recognition, indicating that revenue measurement depends materially on system-generated cost and revenue reports rather than simple invoicing.
- Dependence on the IT control environment for accurate cost and revenue reporting — The audit response covered the IT environment in which the business systems operate, including access controls, program change controls, program development controls and IT operation controls, plus completeness and accuracy over cost and revenue reports generated by the system and application controls over allocation of resources and budgeting that prevent unauthorised recording or changes to costs. A failure in these controls would directly distort reported results.
- Customer concentration in banks and financial institutions for the loyalty business — The auditors record that the Company is engaged in loyalty programmes for various banks and financial institutions. A loyalty business anchored on bank and financial-institution clients is exposed to those clients' procurement cycles, and to regulatory or budgetary changes in the financial sector, over which the Company has no control.
- Single reportable segment concentration — The MD&A states the Company is engaged in a single segment, so there is no diversification buffer: a downturn in the core activity flows through to the whole business.
- Newly listed company with a short public-market compliance track record — The Company completed its IPO and was listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange only on 25.03.2026, six days before the financial year end, and converted from Novus Loyalty Private Limited. Full-year listed-entity governance, disclosure and internal-control discipline is therefore untested over a complete reporting cycle.
- Foreign exchange exposure on export earnings — The Directors' Report discloses foreign exchange earnings from sales alongside foreign exchange outgo, so a portion of revenue is earned in foreign currency and is exposed to rate movement. The report describes no hedging policy.
- Talent attrition and dependence on skilled people in an asset-light services model — The MD&A states the Company recognises people as its most valuable asset and that attrition has been managed below industry benchmarks. In a software and services business with no physical assets, delivery capacity is the workforce, so attrition is a structural rather than incidental risk.
- Risk management is described only in general terms, with no named risk register — The MD&A states risk management is an integral part of the business strategy and that a dedicated team reviews compliance with risk policies, monitors risk tolerance limits and analyses risk exposure, but the report names no specific risk, no tolerance limit and no mitigation for any identified exposure. The internal control system is described as commensurate with the size, nature and operations of the Company.

outlook.body:

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capacity expansion, plant, project or capex programme. Novus Loyalty is an asset-light software services and loyalty-programme company operating from a single corporate office at Udyog Vihar Phase V, Gurugram, and the Directors' Report records 'NA' against every Conservation of Energy line, including capital investment on energy conservation equipment, and 'NA' against every Technology Absorption line, including expenditure on Research & Development and details of technology imported. The only capital event of the year was financing rather than capacity: during the year the Company issued bonus shares and completed an Initial Public Offer, and its shares were listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange on 25.03.2026. No deployment plan for the IPO proceeds, no commissioning or ramp timeline, and no new office, delivery centre or platform build-out is described anywhere in the report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global IT and software demand: companies worldwide are rapidly replacing outdated hardware systems and switching to online, cloud-based software so they can operate from anywhere
- AI-led product enhancement: software is becoming smarter by using tools like artificial intelligence to analyse data instantly, helping businesses make quicker and better decisions
- Retention economics: businesses are realising that keeping a current customer happy with a smart rewards program is much cheaper than spending money to find new ones
- Management states demand for easy-to-use software and digital loyalty tools is higher than ever
- Management describes the year's financial performance as reasonably good and states the Company expects good business and returns in future (Directors' Report, State of Company's Affairs and Future Outlook)
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
